NONE: › historical records of the activities of a country or organization, or history in general
歷史記載；歷史；編年史；年鑑

example: The signing of the Treaty of Rome was the greatest event in the annals of European integration.
《羅馬條約》的簽訂是歐洲一體化進程中最重大的事件。
Quite whether he will go down in the annals of American history (= be considered) as a great leader remains to be seen.
他究竟能否作為一個偉大的領導人而載入美國史冊，人們仍需拭目以待。

NONE: › to make metal or glass soft by heating and then cooling it slowly
› a type of worm whose body is divided into several parts
› to take possession of an area of land or a country, usually by force or without permission
（通常指用武力或擅自）吞併；兼併；強佔
› an extra building added to a larger building

example: Delicate and valuable books are kept in an air-conditioned annexe to the main library.
貴重易損的圖書存放在主圖書館的配樓裡，那裡裝有空調設備。

NONE: › to destroy something completely so that nothing is left

example: a city annihilated by an atomic bomb
被原子彈夷為平地的城市
He was annihilated in the finals of the competition.
在決賽中，他被打了個落花流水。

NONE: B1 the day on which an important event happened in a previous year

example: We always celebrate our wedding anniversary with dinner in an expensive restaurant.
我們總是去豪華飯店就餐來慶祝我們的結婚紀念日。
Tomorrow is the 30th anniversary of the revolution.
明天是革命30週年紀念日。

NONE: › a Latin phrase meaning "in the year of the Lord", the full form of the abbreviation AD, which is used when referring to a year after Jesus Christ was born
（在）耶穌紀元，（在）西元（拉丁語，略作AD）
› UK informal a way of referring to the fact that time is passing and that someone is getting older

example: He was a champion and he refused to be beaten by Anno Domini.
他獲得過冠軍，不甘心被年齡打敗。

NONE: › to add a short explanation or opinion to a text or drawing

example: Annotated editions of Shakespeare's plays help readers to understand old words.
莎士比亞劇作的註釋本可以幫助讀者理解劇中較古老的詞語。

NONE: B1 to make something known or tell people about something officially
› to show that something is going to happen

example: They announced the death of their mother in the local paper.
他們在一家當地報紙上刊登了母親去世的訃告。
She announced the winner of the competition to an excited audience.
她向激動的觀眾宣佈了比賽的獲勝者。
[ + that ] The prime minister has announced that public spending will be increased next year.
首相已經宣佈明年將增加公共開支。
The first few leaves in the gutter announced the beginning of autumn.
排水溝中最先落入的幾片葉子標誌著秋天的來臨。

NONE: B1 something that someone says officially, giving information about something

example: The president made an unexpected announcement this morning.
今天上午總統發表了一項出人意表的聲明。
The announcement of the changes has been delayed.
變革內容公佈的時間推後了。

NONE: › someone who introduces programmes or reads the news on the television or radio
（電視臺或電臺的）節目主持人，廣播員，播音員

example: a radio/TV announcer
電臺／電視節目主持人
Tina really annoyed me in the meeting this morning.
在今天上午的會上，蒂娜真是把我氣壞了。
I'm sorry - is my cough annoying you?
對不起，我咳嗽打擾你了吧？
[ + that ] It annoys me that she just expects us to help.
她只是眼巴巴地指望我們去幫她，我真是氣得慌。
It really annoys me when people expect me to tip as well as pay a service charge in a restaurant.
在飯店裡，付了服務費後他們還想要小費，這很讓我惱火。

NONE: › to make someone extremely annoyed, frightened, etc.
使（某人）極為惱怒／害怕（等等）

example: He jumped out from behind a wall and scared the hell out of her.
他從一道牆後面跳了出來，把她嚇了個半死。

U: C1 [ U ] the feeling or state of being annoyed

C: › [ C ] something that makes you annoyed
令人煩惱的事；令人不快的事

example: I can understand your annoyance - I'd be furious if she ever treated me like that.
我能理解你為甚麼生氣——她要是那樣對我，我也會發火的。
(Much) to our annoyance, (= we were very annoyed that) we couldn't see anything from the back row of the theatre.
讓我們（特別）氣惱的是，坐在劇院的後排，我們甚麼也看不見。
One of the greatest annoyances was being bitten by mosquitoes every night.
最讓人不堪其擾的是，每天晚上都要挨蚊子叮咬。
I was so annoyed with him for turning up late.
他姍姍來遲，我很生氣。
He was annoyed at the way she tried to take over the whole meeting.
她試圖操控整個會議，這使他很惱火。
My parents were rather annoyed (that) I hadn't told them about the accident.
我沒有告訴父母這次事故，這讓他們很生氣。
She was annoyed to discover that her husband had taken her car keys.
她丈夫拿走了她的汽車鎖匙，她發現後很生氣。
It's really annoying when a train is late and there's no explanation.
火車延誤而又不作任何解釋，這很令人惱火。
He's got a really annoying laugh.
他的笑聲真讓人煩。

NONE: B1 relating to a period of one year

C: › a book or magazine published once a year, especially for children, with the same title and style but different contents
年刊，年報；（尤指）兒童年冊
› a plant that grows, produces seeds, and dies within one year

example: an annual event/visit/holiday
年度大事／每年一次的訪問／每年的假期
Companies publish annual reports to inform the public about the previous year's activities.
公司發布年度報告，告知公眾上一年的具體業務。
Compare
biennial adjective

NONE: › a meeting that happens once every year in which a company or other organization discusses the past year's activities and elects new officers
› (of an amount or number) calculated over a year

example: Exports fell at an annualized rate of 12.3 percent, while imports rose at a 7.5 percent pace.
從年度總額來看，出口下降了12.3%，而進口上升了7.5%。
Your starting salary is £23,000 per annum and will be reviewed annually.
你的起薪是每年23000英鎊，以後每年核定一次。

NONE: › a fixed amount of money paid to someone every year, usually until their death, or the insurance agreement or investment that provides the money that is paid
（通常指一直付到某人死亡的）年金；年金保險；年金保險投資

example: an annuity policy
年金保險單
She receives a small annuity.
她每年得到一筆微薄的年金。

NONE: › to officially announce that something such as a law, agreement, or marriage no longer exists
廢除，取消（法律、協議等）；宣佈（婚姻）無效

example: His second marriage was annulled because he never divorced his first wife.
他的第二次婚姻被判無效，因為他從未與第一任妻子離婚。

NONE: › a year of extremely bad events
可怕的一年，多災多難的一年
› a year of extremely good events
奇蹟迭出的一年；令人驚異之年；大吉之年

example: 1969 was the annus mirabilis in which man first landed on the moon.
1969年是充滿奇蹟的一年，這一年人類首次登上月球。
